# Skill-Shipped Hook Registration

A skill that needs a lifecycle hook ships the registration as data next to the
hook script. The config repo for each harness discovers it by glob at reconcile
time and merges it into the file that harness reads.

Supported harnesses: **Claude Code** and **Codex**. No others.

## The Convention

1. Hook script and registration live inside the skill:

   ```text
   my-skill/
   ├── SKILL.md
   └── hooks/
       ├── my-hook.py             # the hook
       ├── register.claude.json   # Claude Code registration
       ├── register.codex.json    # Codex registration
       └── test_my_hook.py        # the hook's self-check
   ```

2. Ship one fragment per harness the hook supports, named
   `register.claude.json` and `register.codex.json`. A fragment contains only
   that skill's hooks, in that harness's hook config shape, and nothing else.
3. Commands point at the installed skill, `~`-relative — never at a
   development checkout. Both fragments point at `~/.claude/skills/<name>/`,
   which is where skills are installed for either harness.
4. Every command ends with a `# KEEP: <reason>` shell comment.
5. The config repo holds no copy of the registration. It globs
   `skills/*/hooks/register.claude.json` (`my-claude-stuff`) or
   `skills/*/hooks/register.codex.json` (`my-codex-stuff`) under the skill
   install root and merges what it finds.
6. Merging unions each event's rule list and deduplicates identical rules. It
   never replaces the list.
7. The skill installs nothing. No postinstall step and no writes to
   `settings.json` or `hooks.json`; `make reconcile` in the config repo is the
   only thing that writes.
8. The skill's tests assert its own markers: present, reason non-empty, and
   commented out rather than passed as an argument.

## Claude Code

Fragment: `hooks/register.claude.json`. Merged into `~/.claude/settings.json`.
Rule entries take a `matcher`.

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "*",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "python3 ~/.claude/skills/commit/hooks/record-attribution.py  # KEEP: records the authoring model for Assisted-by trailers"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "Stop": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "python3 ~/.claude/skills/commit/hooks/record-attribution.py  # KEEP: drops attribution for repos this session left clean"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Codex

Fragment: `hooks/register.codex.json`. Merged into `~/.codex/hooks.json`. Rule
entries carry no `matcher`. The command path still points into
`~/.claude/skills/<name>/`.

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "python3 ~/.claude/skills/commit/hooks/record-attribution.py  # KEEP: records the authoring model for Assisted-by trailers"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "Stop": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "python3 ~/.claude/skills/commit/hooks/record-attribution.py  # KEEP: drops attribution for repos this session left clean"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## The `# KEEP: <reason>` marker

Config-copying tooling drops every hook that does not ask to survive. Opt in
with a marker on the command itself:

- Write it as a shell comment at the end of the command. Not a JSON key on the
  hook object, and not an argument.
- State a reason. A bare `# KEEP` is retained, but tests require the reason.

Mechanics — what a rewrite drops, why a comment survives and an argument
misbehaves — are in
[knowledgebase/claude-code/settings-json-rewrites.md](https://github.com/jewzaam/knowledgebase/blob/main/claude-code/settings-json-rewrites.md).

## When not to use it

- **Plugin-packaged skills.** A plugin declares hooks in its own
  `hooks/hooks.json`, loaded by the harness. See
  [claude-code/plugins.md](../claude-code/plugins.md).
- **Hooks the config repo owns.** A hook whose script lives in the config repo
  belongs in that repo's own settings fragment, not behind this glob.

## Reference implementation

- [jewzaam/claude-skill-commit](https://github.com/jewzaam/claude-skill-commit)
  — `hooks/register.claude.json`, `hooks/register.codex.json`, and the hook they
  register.
- `my-claude-stuff` — `scripts/reconcile.py`, `SKILL_FRAGMENTS`.
- `my-codex-stuff` — `scripts/reconcile.py`, `SKILL_HOOK_FRAGMENTS`.
